topic: T3: Variational Quantum Eigensolver (VQE) for Molecular Ground States

tasks.physical_system: Hydrogen molecule (H₂), STO-3G minimal basis, equilibrium geometry

scientific_information.geometry: H–H bond length R = 0.735 Å; H₁ at (0,0,0), H₂ at (0,0,0.735) Å
scientific_information.additional_support: Ansatz: Ry(θ₀)⊗Ry(θ₁)→CNOT, 2 params. Chemical accuracy: |ΔE|<1.6×10⁻³ Ha. Qubits: 2.

tasks.prompt: Implement VQE on the provided 2-qubit H₂/STO-3G Hamiltonian. Report all seven required outputs.
tasks.benchmark_rationale: Universal VQE sanity-check baseline; closed-form FCI solution enables unambiguous validation.

canonical_solution.reference_source: FCI/STO-3G exact diagonalisation; nuclear repulsion = 0.7199819 Ha; PySCF + OpenFermion, JW + Z₂ tapering.

pauli_hamiltonian_verified.derivation: PySCF STO-3G RHF → OpenFermion MolecularData → jordan_wigner → 4-qubit form → Z₂ symmetry tapering → 2 qubits

recommended_workflow.step_2: Ansatz: Ry(θ₀)|0⟩ ⊗ Ry(θ₁)|0⟩ → CNOT(0,1). Two free parameters.
recommended_workflow.step_3: Pauli grouping for simultaneous measurement: {Z₀,Z₁,Z₀Z₁}→1 circuit; {X₀X₁}→1; {Y₀Y₁}→1. Total: 3 circuits.
recommended_workflow.step_4: Optimise with COBYLA (maxiter=200); convergence in 50–100 evaluations.

key_scientific_facts: Correlation energy = E_FCI − E_HF = −1.13727 − (−1.11671) = −20.56 mHa.
The 2-qubit tapered Hamiltonian has exactly 6 Pauli terms; the pre-taper JW 4-qubit form has 15 terms.
Chemical accuracy (1 kcal/mol = 1.593 mHa) IS achievable with the minimal 2-parameter Ry–CNOT ansatz.
The optimal ansatz parameter satisfies tan(2θ) = 2×0.18093/(0.39793−(−0.01128)) ≈ 0.879; θ ≈ 0.374 rad.
common_failure_modes: Forgetting the nuclear repulsion offset (0.7199819 Ha) in the Pauli constant term.
Using the 4-qubit pre-tapering form instead of the 2-qubit tapered form.
Reporting HF energy (−1.11671 Ha) instead of FCI (−1.13727 Ha) as the reference.
Measuring all 6 Pauli terms individually (6 circuits) instead of 3 via QWC grouping.

tasks.physical_system: Helium hydride cation (HeH⁺), STO-3G minimal basis, equilibrium geometry

scientific_information.geometry: He–H bond length R = 1.4632 Bohr (0.7743 Å); He at (0,0,0), H at (0,0,0.7743) Å
scientific_information.additional_support: Asymmetric Z₀≠Z₁ coefficients reflect heteronuclear character. Use 3-parameter ansatz.

tasks.prompt: Implement VQE for HeH⁺/STO-3G using the 2-qubit Pauli Hamiltonian. Note the heteronuclear asymmetry.
tasks.benchmark_rationale: HeH⁺ introduces heteronuclear asymmetry (Z₀≠Z₁) absent from H₂, testing whether the solver adapts the ansatz to a non-symmetric Hamiltonian.

canonical_solution.reference_source: FCI/STO-3G exact diagonalisation at R=1.4632 Bohr; nuclear repulsion = +1.3568 Ha. Consistent with Moll et al. 2016 photonic VQE experiment.

pauli_hamiltonian_verified.key_difference_from_H2: Z₀ coefficient (0.20640) ≠ |Z₁| coefficient (0.32658), reflecting He(Z=2) vs H(Z=1) nuclear charges. H₂ has Z₀=−Z₁ by homonuclear symmetry.

recommended_workflow.step_2: Ansatz: Ry(θ₀)|0⟩ ⊗ Ry(θ₁)|0⟩ → CNOT(0,1) → Ry(θ₂) on qubit 0. Three parameters required for heteronuclear system.
recommended_workflow.step_4: Optimise with COBYLA; 100–150 evaluations to convergence.
recommended_workflow.critical_note: A symmetric 2-parameter ansatz (θ₀=θ₁) CANNOT reach FCI energy because Z₀≠Z₁; a minimum of 3 independent parameters is required.

key_scientific_facts: HeH⁺ is the first interstellar molecule detected (2019, SOFIA telescope; Güsten et al., Nature 568, 357).
Correlation energy = −2.86280 − (−2.85523) = −7.57 mHa; smaller than H₂ because He dominates.
The homonuclear X₀X₁=Y₀Y₁=0.18093 coupling persists due to the shared 2-electron structure.
A 2-parameter symmetric ansatz converges to a variational energy above FCI due to the asymmetric diagonal terms.
common_failure_modes: Using a symmetric 2-parameter Ry–CNOT ansatz (identical to H₂ minimal ansatz); this cannot reproduce HeH⁺ FCI energy.
Confusing STO-3G (2 MOs → 2 qubits after tapering) with a larger basis.
Not verifying that the VQE energy lies below the Hartree-Fock energy (−2.85523 Ha).

tasks.physical_system: Hydrogen molecule (H₂), STO-3G basis, stretched geometry (R = 1.5 Å)

scientific_information.hamiltonian: Not provided — solver must construct from PySCF STO-3G integrals at R=1.5 Å.
scientific_information.reference_energy: E_FCI/STO-3G ≈ −0.9831 Ha; E_HF(RHF) ≈ −0.9021 Ha; E_HF(UHF) ≈ −0.9310 Ha. Correlation energy ≈ −81 mHa.

tasks.prompt: Construct the STO-3G Hamiltonian for H₂ at R=1.5 Å, map to qubits, implement VQE with an ansatz capturing strong static correlation. Report all seven required outputs.
tasks.benchmark_rationale: Tests strong-correlation ansatz design in the S2 setting where no Hamiltonian is provided. Distinguishes from t3_0 by requiring independent Hamiltonian construction and multi-reference reasoning.

canonical_solution.reference_source: FCI/STO-3G at R=1.5 Å; nuclear repulsion = 1/R_Bohr = 1/2.8346 = 0.3528 Ha; PySCF fci.FCI solver.

hamiltonian_construction_guide.step_2: OpenFermion: MolecularData → run_pyscf(run_fci=True) → jordan_wigner → Z₂ taper → 2-qubit form

approximate_Pauli_coefficients_R15A.I_constant_Ha: ≈ −0.88 (varies with implementation; nuclear repulsion already included)
approximate_Pauli_coefficients_R15A.Z0Z1: ≈ −0.28  (note: larger magnitude than at equilibrium, reflecting stronger correlation)
approximate_Pauli_coefficients_R15A.note: Exact values must be computed with PySCF. The key signature of strong correlation is |Z₀Z₁| ≈ |Z₀|.

recommended_workflow.ansatz: UCCSD with 1 double-excitation amplitude θ (1 free parameter). At R=1.5 Å the optimal θ ≈ π/4, giving equal-weight superposition of the two Slater determinants.
recommended_workflow.why_single_reference_fails: At R=1.5 Å: RHF (−0.9021 Ha) is 81 mHa above FCI. The ground state approaches (1/√2)(|01⟩−|10⟩) in the tapered basis — a maximally entangled state that requires θ=π/4 in the UCCSD operator.
recommended_workflow.coulson_fischer_point: Spin-symmetry breaking in RHF occurs at R ≈ 1.2 Å (Coulson-Fischer point); above this, UHF gives a lower energy than RHF.
recommended_workflow.starting_point: Initialise optimiser at θ=π/4 (not θ=0) to avoid the HF local minimum.

key_scientific_facts: R=1.5 Å ≈ 2× equilibrium bond length (0.735 Å), close to the dissociation regime.
The UCCSD ansatz for 2-electron/2-orbital systems EXACTLY reproduces FCI at any geometry (1-parameter problem spans the full Hilbert space).
The optimal UCCSD amplitude at R=1.5 Å is θ ≈ π/4 (50:50 superposition), compared to θ ≈ 0.374 rad at equilibrium.
Chemical accuracy IS achievable with a 1-parameter UCCSD or 2-parameter Ry–CNOT ansatz despite the strong correlation.
common_failure_modes: Using equilibrium-geometry Pauli coefficients instead of computing fresh integrals at R=1.5 Å.
Initialising the optimiser at θ=0 (HF reference) and converging to a local minimum above the true ground state.
Reporting RHF or UHF energy as the VQE result without running the variational loop.

tasks.physical_system: Trihydrogen cation (H₃⁺), STO-3G basis, equilateral triangle geometry

scientific_information.geometry: Equilateral triangle, R_HH = 1.65 Bohr (0.8731 Å); vertices at (0,0.5039,0), (±0.4366,−0.2520,0) Å
scientific_information.basis_set: STO-3G (3 spatial MOs from 3 H 1s AOs)
scientific_information.hamiltonian: 4-qubit Pauli Hamiltonian (JW + Z₂ tapering from 6 spin-orbitals to 4 qubits). ~20–30 significant Pauli terms; exact coefficients must be computed with PySCF/OpenFermion at the specified geometry.
scientific_information.reference_energy: E_FCI/STO-3G ≈ −1.3441 Ha (FCI=exact for 2-electron systems); E_HF/STO-3G ≈ −1.3277 Ha
scientific_information.additional_support: UCCSD with (2e,3o): 1 double + 2 singles = 3 parameters. D₃ₕ symmetry: ground state is A₁' (totally symmetric). Restrict ansatz to Sz=0, N_e=2 sector.

tasks.prompt: Using the described 4-qubit H₃⁺/STO-3G Hamiltonian (compute exact Pauli coefficients with PySCF), implement VQE exploiting D₃ₕ symmetry. Report all seven required outputs.
tasks.benchmark_rationale: First polyatomic system in the benchmark. Introduces 3-centre molecular orbitals, D₃ₕ symmetry, and a multi-parameter UCCSD ansatz at 4 qubits.

canonical_solution.reference_source: FCI/STO-3G = CISD = CCSD for 2-electron systems (exact regardless of orbital count). PySCF cisd solver. Nuclear repulsion = 3/R_HH_bohr = 3/1.65 = 1.8182 Ha.

hamiltonian_construction_guide.key_point: charge=+1 for H₃⁺ (2 electrons in 3-proton system)
hamiltonian_construction_guide.symmetry_note: D₃ₕ symmetry enforces equal coefficients for symmetry-equivalent Pauli strings (e.g., hopping between the two 1e' orbitals)

recommended_workflow.ansatz: UCCSD: θ_d (1a₁'→1e' double excitation) + θ_s1, θ_s2 (single excitations). 3 parameters total.
recommended_workflow.pauli_grouping: QWC grouping of 20–30 terms → 5–8 distinct measurement circuits
recommended_workflow.optimiser: BFGS with parameter-shift gradients or COBYLA; 3-parameter UCCSD converges in <50 iterations

key_scientific_facts: H₃⁺ is the most abundant polyatomic ion in the universe and dominant species in cold molecular clouds.
FCI = CISD = CCSD for any 2-electron system; the only approximation is the STO-3G basis set.
The doubly-degenerate 1e' LUMO means the single double excitation 1a₁'→1e' fully spans the correlation space.
Correlation energy = −1.3441 − (−1.3277) = −16.4 mHa, comparable to H₂ at equilibrium.
common_failure_modes: Setting charge=0 instead of charge=+1 in PySCF mol (H₃⁺ has +1 charge, 2 electrons).
Confusing the equilateral geometry with a linear H–H–H arrangement.
Not tapering the 6-qubit JW form to 4 qubits.

tasks.physical_system: Two-site Fermi-Hubbard model at half-filling (t=1, U=4)

scientific_information.geometry: 2 lattice sites, open boundary; N_e=2 (half-filling: N↑=N↓=1). t=1, U=4.
scientific_information.basis_set: Single-band Hubbard model: H = −t Σ(c†c+h.c.) + U Σ n↑n↓
scientific_information.hamiltonian: 4-qubit JW [site1↑,site1↓,site2↑,site2↓]: H = (U/4)(I−Z₀Z₁) + (U/4)(I−Z₂Z₃) − (t/2)(X₀Z₁X₂+Y₀Z₁Y₂) − (t/2)(X₁X₃+Y₁Y₃). With t=1,U=4: on-site coeff=1.0, hopping coeff=0.5.
scientific_information.additional_support: Restrict ansatz to N_e=2, S_z=0 sector. 3–4 measurement circuits total.

tasks.prompt: Implement VQE for the 2-site Hubbard model (t=1, U=4). Preserve particle-number and spin symmetry. Compare to exact analytical reference E₀=2−2√2≈-0.82843. Report all seven required outputs.
tasks.benchmark_rationale: Exact analytical reference (E₀=2−2√2) makes validation unambiguous. Tests lattice-model VQE, particle-number conservation, and the Jordan-Wigner string in the hopping term.

canonical_solution.reference_source: Exact analytical: E₀ = (U − √(U²+16t²))/2 = (4−√32)/2 = 2−2√2 = -0.82842712 (in units of t). Verified by exact diagonalisation of the 6-state half-filling sector.

analytical_derivation.singlet_sector_matrix: 2×2 matrix: [[0, −√2t], [−√2t, U]] in the {|↑↓,0⟩, |0,↑↓⟩, singlet} reduced basis

pauli_hamiltonian_verified.jw_string_note: The term X₀Z₁X₂ contains the JW string Z₁ from the fermionic anticommutation between the ↓-spin orbital and the ↑-spin of site 2.

recommended_workflow.initial_state: |1100⟩ (JW: site1↑=1, site1↓=0, site2↑=1, site2↓=0) or |0110⟩ for the (N↑=1,N↓=1) sector
recommended_workflow.ansatz: Particle-number-conserving Givens rotation between |↑↓,0⟩ and |0,↑↓⟩ components plus triplet-singlet mixing term. Or: hardware-efficient with symmetry constraints.

validation_criteria.lattice_model_note: Molecular chemical accuracy (1.6 mHa) does not apply; use |ΔE| < 0.001t = 0.001 as the lattice analogue.

key_scientific_facts: Exact ground-state energy: E₀ = 2 − 2√2 = -0.82842712 (in units of t=1).
Exact first-excited singlet: E₁ = 2 + 2√2 = 4.828427; gap = 5.656854t.
At U=0 (free electrons): E₀ = −2t = −2.0 (both electrons in the bonding orbital).
At U→∞ (Mott insulator): E₀ → −4t²/U = −1.0 (Heisenberg antiferromagnet limit).
U/t=4 is intermediate coupling: metallic but with significant correlation (E₀ = −0.828 vs free-electron −2.0).
The JW string Z₁ in X₀Z₁X₂ arises because the ↑-spin hop from site 1 to site 2 must anticommute past the ↓-spin orbital at site 1.
common_failure_modes: Dropping the Jordan-Wigner string (Z₁) from the hopping terms X₀Z₁X₂ and Y₀Z₁Y₂.
Forgetting the constant energy offset (2×U/4 = U/2 = 2.0) from the on-site terms.
Not restricting the ansatz to the N_e=2 sector.
Reporting energy in wrong units (the reference is already in units of t=1).

tasks.physical_system: Lithium hydride (LiH), STO-3G basis, equilibrium geometry, frozen-core

scientific_information.geometry: Li–H bond length R = 1.5957 Å; Li at (0,0,0), H at (0,0,1.5957) Å
scientific_information.basis_set: STO-3G (6 spatial MOs: 5 from Li 1s,2s,2p; 1 from H 1s)
scientific_information.hamiltonian: Not provided. Solver must construct frozen-core (4e,5o) active-space Hamiltonian.
scientific_information.reference_energy: Full FCI/STO-3G: −7.8824 Ha; Frozen-core FCI: −7.8786 Ha; RHF: −7.8631 Ha. Core correlation ≈ 3.8 mHa.

tasks.prompt: Construct the STO-3G frozen-core Hamiltonian for LiH (freeze Li 1s core), reduce to ≤6 qubits, implement VQE, and report all seven required outputs.
tasks.benchmark_rationale: Reproduces the first 6-qubit VQE hardware experiment (Kandala 2017). Tests frozen-core active-space construction and ionic-bond ansatz design at S2 support.

canonical_solution.reference_source: Kandala et al., Nature 549, 242 (2017); PySCF CASCI at R=1.5957 Å, STO-3G. Nuclear repulsion = 2.0066 Ha.

active_space_description.frozen_orbital: MO 0 (Li 1s core, lowest energy); 2 frozen electrons
tapering_symmetries: Spatial parity symmetry of C∞v LiH: removes 2 more qubits

hamiltonian_construction_guide.step_2: Identify core orbital: MO 0 (lowest energy, Li 1s character). Set freeze_core=True or active=[1,2,3,4,5].
hamiltonian_construction_guide.step_3: Build MolecularHamiltonian with frozen core → OpenFermion → jordan_wigner → 10-qubit raw form
hamiltonian_construction_guide.bravyi_kitaev_note: BK transform gives sparser Hamiltonian than JW for 10 spin-orbitals; either is acceptable.

recommended_workflow.ansatz: UCCSD in (4e,5o): 6 double excitations + 4 single excitations = 10 parameters. Or hardware-efficient 6-qubit with 2 CNOT layers (12 Ry params).
recommended_workflow.ionic_character: LiH is ionic (Li⁺H⁻) at equilibrium. Dominant config >98% closed-shell → UCCSD is sufficient (no multi-reference needed at equilibrium).
recommended_workflow.optimiser: BFGS or COBYLA with 10 parameters; converges in 200–500 evaluations

energy_error_vs_full_fci_Ha.note: Core correlation (3.8 mHa) is irreducible without unfreezing the core

validation_criteria.full_fci_note: If comparing to full FCI (−7.8824 Ha), expect a 3.8 mHa systematic error from core freezing.

key_scientific_facts: LiH is one of four molecules in the Kandala et al. 2017 Nature VQE paper.
The Li 1s core orbital lies 2.4 Ha below the valence orbitals; freezing it introduces a core-correlation error of ≈3.8 mHa.
LiH is weakly correlated at equilibrium: the dominant Slater determinant weight >98%. UCCSD is sufficient.
At R ≈ 3.02 Å (twice equilibrium), LiH dissociates to Li⁰ + H⁰ and becomes strongly correlated.
The (4e,5o) frozen-core active space has C(10,4)=210 determinants; symmetry reduction makes the effective dimension much smaller.
common_failure_modes: Using 5 active electrons instead of 4 (the frozen Li 1s accounts for 2 electrons).
Not applying qubit tapering, leaving an unnecessary 10-qubit Hamiltonian.
Comparing the active-space energy to full FCI without accounting for the 3.8 mHa core offset.
Using bond length in Bohr instead of Angstrom (1.5957 Å ≠ 1.5957 Bohr).

tasks.physical_system: Linear hydrogen chain H₄, STO-3G basis, equal spacing R = 1.5 Bohr

scientific_information.hamiltonian: Not provided. Solver must compute the 8-qubit JW Hamiltonian using PySCF and OpenFermion at the specified STO-3G geometry. No tapering applied; retain the full 8-qubit form. Expected: ~30–50 significant Pauli terms.
scientific_information.reference_energy: E_FCI/STO-3G ≈ −2.0452 Ha; E_HF/STO-3G ≈ −2.0200 Ha. Correlation energy ≈ −25 mHa.
scientific_information.additional_support: UCCSD with 8 parameters; note UCCSD may not achieve chemical accuracy due to near-degenerate HOMO/LUMO. Consider UCCGSD or deeper circuits.

tasks.prompt: Compute H₄/STO-3G Pauli coefficients with PySCF, implement 8-qubit VQE, assess UCCSD adequacy, and report all seven required outputs including Pauli grouping measurement cost.
tasks.benchmark_rationale: First 8-qubit system in the benchmark. Tests UCCSD adequacy assessment (a critical scientific reasoning discriminator) and Pauli grouping for a denser Hamiltonian.

canonical_solution.reference_source: FCI/STO-3G at equal spacing R=1.5 Bohr; PySCF fci.FCI. Nuclear repulsion: 6 H-H pairs: (1/1.5)×3 + (1/3.0)×2 + (1/4.5)×1 = 2.000+0.667+0.222 = 2.889 Ha (approximate; exact via pyscf).

active_space_description.tapering_note: Task specifies no tapering; 8 qubits retained to expose full JW structure.
active_space_description.orbital_character: 4 MOs from 4 H 1s AOs: σ₁ (bonding), σ₂ (weakly bonding), σ₃ (weakly antibonding), σ₄ (antibonding) in D∞h symmetry

correlation_analysis.reasoning: HOMO-LUMO gap at equal spacing ≈ 0.3–0.5 Ha; moderate multi-reference character from near-degenerate σ₂/σ₃ pair. UCCSD misses 3-body correlation contributions.

hamiltonian_construction_guide.step_1: PySCF: mol=gto.M(atom='H 0 0 0; H 0 0 0.7937; H 0 0 1.5874; H 0 0 2.3812', basis='sto-3g', unit='Angstrom')
hamiltonian_construction_guide.approximate_structure: 8 diagonal Zᵢ terms + O(28) off-diagonal ZZ, XX, YY, and longer Pauli strings

recommended_workflow.uccgsd_ansatz: Generalised doubles: O(N²) singles + O(N⁴) doubles, pruned by symmetry to ~20–30 params
recommended_workflow.pauli_grouping: QWC grouping → approximately 8–12 distinct measurement circuits
recommended_workflow.optimiser: BFGS for UCCSD; COBYLA for hardware-efficient 3-layer ansatz

energy_error_Ha.note: UCCSD typically outside chemical accuracy for H₄; UCCGSD or 3-layer HEA achieves it

validation_criteria.ansatz_reasoning: result must state whether UCCSD achieves chemical accuracy and justify

key_scientific_facts: H₄ at equal spacing is a model for the Peierls transition: equal spacing ≈ metallic, alternating spacing drives dimerisation.
UCCSD error for H₄ at equal spacing: typically 2–4 mHa (1–2.5× chemical accuracy threshold).
UCCGSD (generalised doubles) reduces the error to <1 mHa and achieves chemical accuracy.
Nuclear repulsion for linear H₄ at R=1.5 Bohr: 6 pairs → E_nuc = 3/1.5 + 2/3.0 + 1/4.5 = 2 + 0.667 + 0.222 = 2.889 Ha.
The 8-qubit JW Hamiltonian has at most C(8,2)×... possible Pauli strings, but symmetry reduces significant terms to ~30–50.
common_failure_modes: Using coordinates in Angstrom instead of Bohr (1.5 Bohr = 0.7937 Å; adjust unit in PySCF accordingly).
Claiming UCCSD achieves chemical accuracy without numerical verification.
Using 4 instead of 8 qubits (the task explicitly requests no tapering).
Confusing the H₄ linear chain with the H₄ ring or square.

tasks.physical_system: Water molecule (H₂O), STO-3G basis, equilibrium geometry, (2e,2o) active space

scientific_information.basis_set: STO-3G (7 spatial MOs: 5 occupied + 2 virtual from RHF); active space: HOMO (1b₁) + LUMO (4a₁)
scientific_information.hamiltonian: Not provided. Solver must construct (2e,2o) CAS Hamiltonian.

tasks.prompt: Construct the H₂O (2e,2o) CAS Hamiltonian at STO-3G/equilibrium geometry, map to ≤4 qubits, implement VQE, and report all seven required outputs. Discuss what fraction of total FCI correlation is captured.
tasks.benchmark_rationale: Tests active-space selection for water, a fundamental skill in practical quantum chemistry. Requires the solver to distinguish CAS-FCI from full-FCI references and reason about active-space completeness.

canonical_solution.reference_source: PySCF CASSCF(2,2)/STO-3G at C₂v equilibrium geometry; nuclear repulsion = 9.1888 Ha.

active_space_description.homo: MO 4 (1b₁): O lone-pair p_z orbital perpendicular to the molecular plane
active_space_description.mathematical_equivalence: The (2e,2o) CAS for H₂O has identical mathematical structure to H₂/STO-3G in the 2-qubit tapered representation; only Hamiltonian coefficients differ.

hamiltonian_construction_guide.step_1: PySCF: mol=gto.M(atom='O 0 0 0; H 0.757 0.586 0; H -0.757 0.586 0', basis='sto-3g'); RHF → canonical MOs
hamiltonian_construction_guide.step_2: Identify HOMO (MO index 4, 1b₁ in C₂v) and LUMO (MO index 5, 4a₁)
hamiltonian_construction_guide.step_3: Extract (2e,2o) CAS integrals for {HOMO, LUMO}; build FermionOperator from 4 spin-orbital integrals
hamiltonian_construction_guide.step_4: JW transform → 4 qubits → taper to 2 qubits (same procedure as H₂)

recommended_workflow.ansatz: 1-parameter Ry–CNOT circuit (identical structure to H₂ minimal ansatz; 2e in 2 orbitals is always a 1-parameter problem after tapering)
recommended_workflow.optimiser: Can be solved analytically: E(θ) = a + b·cos(θ); minimise analytically or use 1D golden-section search

energy_error_vs_full_fci_Ha.explanation: (2e,2o) active space captures only 10% of total FCI correlation; 2.7 mHa error floor is irreducible

validation_criteria.bounds_check: result['ground_state_energy_estimate'] > -74.9656  # Must be above full FCI
validation_criteria.active_space_discussion: result must discuss the 10% correlation-capture limitation and why chemical accuracy vs full FCI is unachievable

key_scientific_facts: The (2e,2o) CAS captures only 10% of H₂O total correlation; a (6e,5o) space covering all valence orbitals would capture ~95%.
The H₂O STO-3G basis has 7 MOs and 10 electrons; only the (2e,2o) HOMO-LUMO pair fits in ≤4 qubits.
The 1b₁ HOMO is the oxygen lone-pair orbital perpendicular to the molecular plane — the highest-occupied MO in water.
A (6e,5o) H₂O active space would require 10 qubits — just within the benchmark limit; a (6e,4o) space requires 8 qubits.
The (2e,2o) ansatz is mathematically a 1-parameter trigonometric problem: E(θ) = a + b cos(θ) + c sin(θ).
common_failure_modes: Confusing the HOMO: the 1b₁ is the O lone-pair (not 3a₁ which is slightly lower in energy in STO-3G).
Claiming chemical accuracy vs full FCI (−74.9656 Ha) — impossible with (2e,2o) active space due to 2.7 mHa systematic truncation error.
Using a deep multi-parameter ansatz for a 1-parameter problem (wastes circuit depth).
Counting 10 electrons as active instead of just the 2 in the active space.

tasks.physical_system: Beryllium hydride (BeH₂), STO-3G basis, linear equilibrium geometry, (2e,3o) active space

scientific_information.basis_set: STO-3G (9 spatial MOs from Be 1s,2s,2p + 2×H 1s); 5 occupied + 4 virtual MOs
scientific_information.hamiltonian: 6-qubit Pauli Hamiltonian for the (2e,3o) active space. ~40–60 significant terms. Solver must compute exact coefficients with PySCF/OpenFermion at the specified geometry.
scientific_information.additional_support: Compare: (A) UCCSD with 3 parameters vs (B) hardware-efficient Ry–CNOT brickwork with 1–2 layers. Follow Kandala et al. 2017 approach.

tasks.prompt: Compare UCCSD and hardware-efficient ansätze for BeH₂/STO-3G (2e,3o) at 6 qubits. Report all seven required outputs for the better approach. Include a comparison table of both ansätze.
tasks.benchmark_rationale: Reproduces the 6-qubit IBM VQE demonstration from Kandala et al. 2017. Explicitly requires ansatz comparison to test circuit-depth-vs-expressibility reasoning.

canonical_solution.reference_source: Kandala et al., Nature 549, 242 (2017); PySCF CASCI(2,3)/STO-3G at R=1.3264 Å. Nuclear repulsion = 3.1736 Ha.

active_space_description.frozen_orbitals: MO 0 (Be 1s) and MO 1 (Be–H σg bonding 2s-like). 4 frozen electrons.
active_orbital_descriptions: MO 2 (σg bonding): primarily Be 2s with H 1s symmetric combination
MO 3 (non-bonding or 2pz-like Be): the Be 2s-2p near-degeneracy orbital
MO 4 (σu* antibonding): primarily Be 2s − H 1s antisymmetric combination
active_space_description.be_2s_2p_near_degeneracy: The Be 2s and 2p orbitals are nearly degenerate; the ground state has ~15% 2p character requiring at least a 3-orbital active space.

uccsd.reason_for_failure: Be 2s-2p near-degeneracy creates multi-determinant ground state requiring more than 1 double + 2 singles to capture

hardware_efficient_1layer.architecture: Alternating Ry rotations + CNOT ladder, 1 repetition across 6 qubits

hardware_efficient_2layers.architecture: Alternating Ry rotations + CNOT ladder, 2 repetitions
hardware_efficient_2layers.recommendation: This is the Kandala et al. 2017 recommended approach for BeH₂

validation_criteria.comparison_required: result must include explicit comparison of UCCSD vs hardware-efficient ansatz

key_scientific_facts: BeH₂ at 6 qubits is the benchmark system from the landmark Kandala et al. Nature 2017 VQE hardware paper.
The Be 2s-2p near-degeneracy means the ground state has ~15% Be 2p² character: |ψ⟩ ≈ 0.94|σg²⟩ + 0.24(|2px²⟩+|2py²⟩+|2pz²⟩)/√3.
UCCSD with 3 parameters typically fails to reach chemical accuracy for BeH₂ due to this multi-reference character.
The hardware-efficient 2-layer ansatz (Kandala's approach) with 18 parameters typically achieves chemical accuracy.
Full FCI/STO-3G (−15.5373 Ha) differs from CAS(2,3) (−15.5329 Ha) by 4.4 mHa; missing correlation is in frozen core and virtual orbitals.
common_failure_modes: Defining the active space as (2e,2o) instead of (2e,3o); BeH₂ requires 3 orbitals due to the Be 2s-2p near-degeneracy.
Using only 1 HEA layer and claiming chemical accuracy without verifying.
Forgetting to freeze 4 core electrons (2 from Be 1s + 2 from Be-H σg bonding MO).
Not recognising that UCCSD underperforms hardware-efficient for BeH₂ and failing to explore deeper ansätze.

tasks.physical_system: Nitrogen molecule (N₂), STO-3G basis, equilibrium geometry, (6e,6o) active space

scientific_information.basis_set: STO-3G (10 spatial MOs: 5 per N from 1s,2s,2p AOs)
scientific_information.hamiltonian: Not provided. Solver must construct (6e,6o) active-space Hamiltonian and reduce to ≤10 qubits.

tasks.prompt: Construct N₂ (6e,6o)/STO-3G Hamiltonian (≤10 qubits after tapering), implement a multi-reference VQE workflow, explain why UCCSD is insufficient for the triple bond, and report all seven required outputs.
tasks.benchmark_rationale: Most challenging molecular task: 10-qubit active space, triple-bond multi-reference character, and S2 support requiring independent construction. Tests advanced ansatz selection beyond UCCSD.

canonical_solution.reference_source: PySCF CASSCF(6,6)/STO-3G at R=1.098 Å; nuclear repulsion = 5.1932 Ha.

active_space_description.frozen_orbitals: MOs 0–3: 1σg (N 1s bonding), 1σu (N 1s antibonding), 2σg (N 2s bonding), 2σu (N 2s antibonding). 8 frozen electrons.
active_space_description.tapering_applied: Particle-number (N_e=6) + S_z=0 + D∞h spatial parity (g/u) → removes 2 qubits: 12→10

leading_ci_coefficients.smaller_terms: Multiple additional double excitations with coefficients 0.05–0.10

multi_reference_analysis.multi_determinant_weight: ~25% of the wavefunction is in non-dominant determinants
multi_reference_analysis.reason: The N₂ triple bond requires simultaneous σ and π antibonding excitations not captured by the single-reference UCCSD operator

hamiltonian_construction_guide.step_2: Freeze MOs 0–3 (4 lowest energy MOs: core and 2s-derived). Active: MOs 4–9.
hamiltonian_construction_guide.step_3: CASCI Hamiltonian for (6e,6o) → OpenFermion → JW → 12-qubit raw form
hamiltonian_construction_guide.step_4: Apply Z₂ tapering for particle-number, S_z, D∞h parity → 10-qubit form

recommended_workflow.ansatz_choice: UCCGSD or ADAPT-VQE (standard UCCSD is insufficient for N₂ triple bond)
recommended_workflow.adapt_vqe_details: ADAPT-VQE builds the ansatz iteratively from a Pauli pool; typically reaches chemical accuracy in 20–50 ADAPT cycles for N₂
recommended_workflow.k_upccgsd: k-UpCCGSD with k=2 is a good alternative: fixed structure, ~50 parameters, reaches near-chemical accuracy

energy_error_vs_cas66_Ha.note: ADAPT-VQE or UCCGSD required for chemical accuracy

validation_criteria.uccsd_reasoning: result must explicitly explain why UCCSD is insufficient for N₂ triple bond

key_scientific_facts: The N₂ triple bond (bond order 3) consists of one σ and two π bonds from N 2p orbitals.
CCSD fails for N₂ at stretched geometries (R > 2.5 Å); CCSD(T) also fails. Multi-reference methods required.
UCCSD error for N₂ (6e,6o) at equilibrium is ~10 mHa, much larger than chemical accuracy (1.6 mHa).
ADAPT-VQE with 20–50 cycles typically achieves chemical accuracy for N₂ by adaptively selecting the most important excitation operators.
The D∞h symmetry of N₂ enforces doubly-degenerate πu and πg* orbitals; the STO-3G basis slightly lifts this degeneracy.
common_failure_modes: Freezing only 2 core orbitals (1s on each N) instead of 4 (must also freeze the 2s-derived σg and σu MOs).
Using UCCSD and claiming chemical accuracy without numerical verification.
Not applying Z₂ symmetry tapering, leaving 12 qubits instead of 10.
Confusing the active MOs (triple bond, indices 4–9) with the frozen core (indices 0–3).

tasks.physical_system: Four-site Fermi-Hubbard model (1D ring), half-filling, U/t = 4

scientific_information.geometry: 4 sites on a ring (PBC); N↑=N↓=2 half-filling; t=1, U=4
scientific_information.basis_set: Single-band Hubbard model; JW ordering [s1↑,s1↓,s2↑,s2↓,s3↑,s3↓,s4↑,s4↓] → 8 qubits
scientific_information.hamiltonian: 8-qubit JW Hamiltonian with PBC. ~32 Pauli terms. Solver must compute exact coefficients with OpenFermion.
scientific_information.reference_energy: E₀ ≈ −2.8762 (Bethe Ansatz / exact diagonalisation, units of t=1)
scientific_information.additional_support: PBC introduces long-range JW string across the ring boundary. Bethe Ansatz reference available for any t, U.

tasks.prompt: Implement 8-qubit VQE for the 4-site ring Hubbard model (t=1, U=4) with correct PBC JW strings. Restrict ansatz to N_e=4, N↑=N↓=2 sector. Discuss PBC vs OBC gate-count impact. Report all seven required outputs.
tasks.benchmark_rationale: Tests PBC Jordan-Wigner implementation and Bethe Ansatz validation. The long-range boundary JW string nearly doubles the two-qubit gate count vs OBC, a critical hardware-awareness test.

canonical_solution.reference_source: Exact diagonalisation of the 4-site half-filling ring sector (70-state Hilbert space). Bethe Ansatz (Lieb-Wu equations) for U=4, t=1, L=4, N=4.

exact_ed_derivation.finite_size_correction: 6-site result is ≈25% above thermodynamic limit due to L=4 boundary effects

pbc_boundary_terms.description: Hopping between site 4 (qubits 6,7) and site 1 (qubits 0,1) requires JW string crossing all intermediate qubits
pbc_boundary_terms.spin_up_pbc: −(t/2)(X₆Z₇Z₀Z₁Z₂Z₃Z₄Z₅X₀ + Y₆Z₇Z₀Z₁Z₂Z₃Z₄Z₅Y₀) — but this is wrong: it is X₆·[JW-string]·X₀ where the string crosses qubits 7,0,1,2,3,4,5 in the JW ordering
pbc_boundary_terms.corrected_pbc_up: The ↑-spin hop from site 4 to site 1 in JW ordering: coefficient −t/2, Pauli weight = 7 (spans qubits 0,2,4,6 with ZZ strings between them)
pbc_boundary_terms.corrected_pbc_down: The ↓-spin hop from site 4 to site 1: coefficient −t/2, Pauli weight = 5
pbc_boundary_terms.gate_count_overhead: Each weight-W Pauli string requires W-1 two-qubit (CNOT) gates in a ladder decomposition
pbc_boundary_terms.pbc_vs_obc_overhead: PBC adds 2 extra Pauli strings of weight 5–7 vs OBC strings of weight 3; adds ~8–12 additional CNOT gates

recommended_workflow.initial_state: |11001100⟩ (JW: site1 ↑↓ occupied, site2 ↑↓ occupied, sites 3,4 empty) — or any N_e=4, N↑=N↓=2 state
recommended_workflow.ansatz: Symmetry-conserving 8-qubit ansatz in the N↑=N↓=2, k=0 (zero-momentum) sector. UCCSD-style hopping + on-site operators adapted to the Hubbard lattice.
recommended_workflow.pbc_note: The PBC hopping terms require long JW strings; include them explicitly in the circuit or the energy will be wrong (effectively simulating OBC instead of PBC).

validation_criteria.pbc_discussion: result must discuss PBC JW string length and gate-count comparison to OBC

key_scientific_facts: The 4-site Hubbard ring at half-filling, U=4, t=1: exact ground-state energy E₀ ≈ −2.8762 in units of t (exact diagonalisation of 70-state half-filling sector).
PBC introduces a hopping term between site L and site 1 that generates a weight-(2L-1) Pauli string in JW ordering, the lattice analogue of a long-range molecular exchange integral.
For L=4 with 8 qubits, the PBC ↑-spin boundary hop generates a weight-7 Pauli string; the ↓-spin generates weight-5.
The Bethe Ansatz (Lieb-Wu equations) gives the exact thermodynamic-limit energy: E₀/L → varies with U/t; at U=4 in TDL: E₀/L ≈ −0.5736.
Finite-size effects are large for L=4: the L=4 result (E₀/L = −0.7190) is 25% above the thermodynamic limit (−0.5736), reflecting the large boundary effects in a 4-site ring.
common_failure_modes: Using OBC hopping (omitting the site4→site1 boundary hop) — this simulates a chain, not a ring.
Dropping the long-range JW strings in the PBC boundary terms, giving an incorrect Hamiltonian.
Not restricting the ansatz to the N_e=4 sector.
Comparing to the thermodynamic-limit Bethe Ansatz energy (−0.5736 per site) instead of the L=4 finite-size result (−0.7190 per site).

tasks.physical_system: Hydrogen fluoride (HF), STO-3G basis, equilibrium geometry, (2e,2o) active space

scientific_information.basis_set: STO-3G (6 spatial MOs; 10 electrons; 5 occupied + 1 virtual)
scientific_information.hamiltonian: Not provided. Solver must construct and justify (2e,2o) CAS Hamiltonian for this 10-electron polar molecule.

tasks.prompt: Construct the HF (2e,2o)/STO-3G active-space Hamiltonian, justify orbital selection for this polar molecule, implement VQE, discuss basis-set scaling, and report all seven required outputs.
tasks.benchmark_rationale: Tests active-space selection for a strongly polar 10-electron molecule where the HOMO identity is non-trivial. S2 level requires independent reasoning about which orbitals to activate.

canonical_solution.reference_source: PySCF CASCI(2,2)/STO-3G at R=0.917 Å; nuclear repulsion = 5.2517 Ha.

active_space_description.homo_orbital: MO 4 (3a₁): F–H σ-bonding orbital with predominantly F 2p_z character (HOMO in STO-3G)
active_space_description.orbital_selection_rationale: The 3a₁ σ-bonding and 4a₁ σ* antibonding MOs directly represent the H–F bond being probed. The F lone pairs (1b₁, 1b₂, MOs 2,3) are frozen because at equilibrium they are barely involved in the bonding correlation.

active_space_limits.to_capture_90pct: Would need (6e,4o) space including F lone pairs → 8 qubits

hamiltonian_construction_guide.step_1: PySCF: mol=gto.M(atom='F 0 0 0; H 0 0 0.917', basis='sto-3g'); RHF → check MO symmetry labels in C∞v
hamiltonian_construction_guide.step_2: Identify HOMO (MO 4, 3a₁, σ-type F-H bonding) and LUMO (MO 5, 4a₁, σ* antibonding)
hamiltonian_construction_guide.step_3: Extract (2e,2o) CAS integrals from RHF MO basis; build FermionOperator for 4 spin-orbitals
hamiltonian_construction_guide.step_4: JW transform → 4 qubits → Z₂ taper → 2 qubits
hamiltonian_construction_guide.mathematical_structure: Identical in form to H₂/STO-3G 2-qubit Hamiltonian; only coefficients differ

6_31G_star.note: At 6-31G* a (6e,4o) active space captures F lone-pair correlation AND fits in 10 qubits after tapering (8 spin-orbitals → ≤8 qubits)

basis_set_scalability_discussion.implication: (2e,2o) active space is basis-set-independent in qubit count but captures increasingly less correlation as the basis improves

recommended_workflow.ansatz: 1-parameter Ry–CNOT (same minimal ansatz as H₂; the (2e,2o) CAS is always a 1-parameter problem after tapering)
recommended_workflow.polar_molecule_note: HF has a large dipole moment (1.826 D); the HOMO (3a₁) has >90% F character, meaning the correlation is dominated by H→F electron transfer — which the (2e,2o) space captures adequately within its limited active space

energy_error_vs_full_fci_Ha.note: 92% of total correlation is outside the (2e,2o) active space

validation_criteria.bounds_check: result['ground_state_energy_estimate'] > -98.5878  # Must be above full FCI
validation_criteria.active_space_justification: result must explain why the F lone pairs are excluded and what the 8% correlation capture means

key_scientific_facts: HF is the most electronegative diatomic molecule (F electronegativity = 3.98 on Pauling scale), creating 91% ionic character at equilibrium.
The STO-3G HOMO-LUMO gap for HF is ~0.7 Ha — very large, reflecting the stability of the closed-shell ionic bond. The (2e,2o) correlation is only 1.4 mHa.
The three F lone pairs (2s-type 2a₁, and the degenerate 1b₁+1b₂ pair) carry 92% of the total correlation energy in HF.
A (6e,4o) active space adding the two degenerate F lone pairs (1b₁, 1b₂) to {3a₁, 4a₁} would capture ~85% of total correlation and requires 8 qubits.
At stretched geometries (R > 1.5 Å), the 3a₁ σ bond breaks and the (2e,2o) space becomes the dominant correlation source — increasing the importance of the HOMO-LUMO active space.
common_failure_modes: Selecting the wrong HOMO: in STO-3G HF, the HOMO is 3a₁ (σ-bonding), not the degenerate 1b₁/1b₂ lone pairs which are at the same energy in large basis sets but not in STO-3G.
Claiming chemical accuracy vs full FCI (−98.5878 Ha) with only (2e,2o) space (impossible; 15.7 mHa systematic floor).
Forgetting that 10 total electrons in HF means 8 are frozen in the (2e,2o) active space.
Not discussing the basis-set scaling point that the prompt explicitly requires.

tasks.physical_system: Transverse-field Ising model (TFIM), 6-site open chain, J=1, h variable

scientific_information.geometry: 6 spin-1/2 sites, open boundary conditions. Study at J/h ∈ {0.5, 1.0, 2.0}.
scientific_information.basis_set: Not applicable. H_TFIM = −J Σᵢ ZᵢZᵢ₊₁ − h Σᵢ Xᵢ
scientific_information.hamiltonian: Not provided. Solver must write the explicit 6-qubit Pauli form and recognise that no JW transform is needed.
scientific_information.reference_energy: Not provided. Solver must compute exact diagonalisation references for each J/h value.

tasks.prompt: Independently formulate the 6-qubit TFIM Hamiltonian (no JW transform needed — spins are already Pauli operators), compute exact-diagonalisation references for all three J/h values, design a near-critical ansatz, run VQE for each, and report all seven required outputs for J/h=1.0 as primary.
tasks.benchmark_rationale: S3 task testing full workflow design for a spin Hamiltonian already in Pauli form. Requires independent reference computation, near-critical ansatz reasoning, and energy landscape analysis.

verified_reference_energies_6site_obc.computation_method: numpy.linalg.eigh of the 64×64 TFIM Hamiltonian matrix; lowest eigenvalue in the full Hilbert space
verified_reference_energies_6site_obc.finite_size_deviation: 6-site OBC critical energy per site (−1.2423) is 2.4% below TDL (−1.2732)

hamiltonian_formulation.key_insight: The TFIM Hamiltonian H = −J Σ ZᵢZᵢ₊₁ − h Σ Xᵢ is already expressed in terms of Pauli operators (Zᵢ = σ_z on qubit i, Xᵢ = σ_x on qubit i). No Jordan-Wigner transformation is needed.

measurement_grouping.group_ZZ: All ZᵢZᵢ₊₁ terms commute → 1 measurement circuit

paramagnetic_phase_h_gt_J.description: Near-product state in the x-basis. Initial state |+⟩⊗6 (all spins aligned with h-field).
paramagnetic_phase_h_gt_J.ansatz: 1 layer of Rz(θᵢ) on each qubit + CNOT ladder: 6+5=11 parameters

ferromagnetic_phase_J_gt_h.description: Near-product state in the z-basis. Ground state approaches |000000⟩ or |111111⟩.
ferromagnetic_phase_J_gt_h.ansatz: GHZ-type preparation: H gate + 5 CNOT cascade → Rz rotations: 6+5=11 parameters

critical_point_J_eq_h.description: Ground state has maximum entanglement; correlation length diverges → barren plateau regime.
critical_point_J_eq_h.recommended_ansatz: QAOA-inspired p=3 layers: exp(−iγ H_ZZ) × exp(−iβ H_X), repeated 3 times. 6 free parameters (γ₁,β₁,γ₂,β₂,γ₃,β₃).
critical_point_J_eq_h.barren_plateau_note: At the critical point, the energy landscape is nearly flat and gradient norms decay with system size. Use random restarts and gradient-free optimisers.
critical_point_J_eq_h.depth_per_layer: 5 ZZ interactions (2 CNOTs each = 10 CNOTs) + 6 Rx gates = 16 gates per p-layer

ansatz_recommendations.general_QAOA_ansatz_depth_recommendation: p=1 for paramagnetic/ferromagnetic; p≥3 for critical

energy_landscape_analysis.paramagnetic: Smooth, convex energy landscape. COBYLA converges in <50 evaluations with p=1.
energy_landscape_analysis.ferromagnetic: Near-degenerate ground state (symmetry broken in TDL). 6-site OBC has a unique GS but very flat landscape near the ferromagnetic minimum.
energy_landscape_analysis.critical_J_eq_h: Barren plateau onset for N≥6: gradient norm ≈ O(1/√(2^N)) → very flat. Expect 5–10× more evaluations than off-critical. Use random restarts.

validation_criteria.exact_diag_required: result must include exact diagonalisation reference values for all three J/h points
validation_criteria.landscape_analysis: result must discuss barren plateau at J/h=1.0

key_scientific_facts: The 1D TFIM is exactly solvable via Jordan-Wigner mapping to free fermions (Pfeuty 1970); the exact critical energy per site in TDL is −4J/π × (integral) ≈ −1.2732J.
For 6-site OBC at J=h=1: E₀ ≈ −7.4536 (exact; compute with numpy.linalg.eigh).
The TFIM Hamiltonian requires NO second quantisation or JW transform — it is already a 2^N × 2^N Hermitian matrix on N qubits via the direct identification Zᵢ↔σ_z^(i), Xᵢ↔σ_x^(i).
QAOA applied to the TFIM is exactly the Trotterised time-evolution of the system; at p→∞ this adiabatically prepares the ground state.
The Z₂ symmetry (global spin flip: Π_i Xᵢ commutes with H) means the ground state is either symmetric or antisymmetric under this transformation; at J≥h the symmetric (+1) sector is the ground state.
common_failure_modes: Applying a Jordan-Wigner transformation (unnecessary for spin models — the Hamiltonian is already Pauli).
Using the thermodynamic-limit critical energy per site (−1.2732) instead of computing the 6-site exact diagonalisation value (−1.2423).
Not recognising the barren plateau at J/h=1 and using p=1 QAOA depth (insufficient for the critical point).
Reporting the energy per site instead of the total energy E₀ (or vice versa without clarity).

tasks.physical_system: Beryllium atom (Be), 6-31G basis, (2e,4o) active space, QPE-inspired workflow

scientific_information.geometry: Atomic system: Be nucleus at (0,0,0); 4 electrons total; freeze 1s² core
scientific_information.basis_set: 6-31G double-zeta (9 basis functions on Be); active space: {2s, 2px, 2py, 2pz} → 4 spatial orbitals, 8 spin-orbitals
scientific_information.hamiltonian: Not provided. Solver must construct (2e,4o) active-space Hamiltonian from PySCF 6-31G integrals.
scientific_information.additional_support: QPE/IQPE or quantum Krylov workflow recommended. Analyse ancilla qubit requirements.

tasks.prompt: Implement IQPE or quantum Krylov workflow for Be (2e,4o)/6-31G on 8 qubits. Discuss ancilla requirements, initial-state overlap, and compare to equivalent VQE. Report all seven required outputs.
tasks.benchmark_rationale: Only QPE/IQPE task in the benchmark, testing a fundamentally different quantum algorithm and its resource tradeoffs vs VQE. The Be 2s-2p near-degeneracy makes initial state preparation non-trivial.

canonical_solution.reference_source: PySCF CASSCF(2,4)/6-31G on Be atom; no nuclear repulsion (atom). Be: Z=4, ground config 1s²2s².

be_2s_2p_near_degeneracy.explanation: In Be, the 2s and 2p orbitals are nearly degenerate due to incomplete nuclear shielding. The true ground state has significant 2p² character.

leading_ci.note: Each 2p component weight: 0.140²≈2%; combined 3×2% = 6% weight in 2p² configurations

hamiltonian_construction_guide.step_1: PySCF: mol=gto.M(atom='Be 0 0 0', basis='6-31g'); RHF → 9 spatial MOs
hamiltonian_construction_guide.step_3: Build CASCI Hamiltonian → OpenFermion → JW → 8-qubit form
hamiltonian_construction_guide.step_4: Taper 2 qubits via particle-number + Sz → 6-qubit form

iqpe_workflow.description: Iterative QPE: 1 ancilla qubit, extract energy bit by bit over m=12 rounds
iqpe_workflow.circuit_per_round: Hadamard on ancilla → controlled-U^(2^k) → Hadamard → measure; k = round index
iqpe_workflow.controlled_U_depth: Trotter decomposition of e^{-iHt}; depth ∝ 2^k × (number of Pauli terms) for round k
iqpe_workflow.total_shots_estimate: 12 rounds × O(1000) repetitions per round ≈ 12,000–50,000 total shots

quantum_krylov_alternative.description: Quantum Krylov subspace diagonalisation: prepare |ψ₀⟩, |e^{-iHt}ψ₀⟩, ..., |e^{-iHKt}ψ₀⟩; classically diagonalise generalised eigenvalue problem
quantum_krylov_alternative.advantage: No ancilla needed; 5 time-evolution circuits + 5 overlap measurements; total ~5000 shots
quantum_krylov_alternative.circuit_depth_per_step: O(50 × T_trotter) for 1 Trotter step of the (2e,4o) Be Hamiltonian

vqe_comparison.verdict: QPE/Krylov is shot-efficient for small systems; advantage grows with required precision. VQE is more practical on NISQ hardware due to shorter circuits.

circuit_depth_iqpe_last_round.note: O(2^11 × T_U) where T_U is Trotter depth; very deep for exact QPE

gate_count_iqpe_total.note: O(100,000) gates across all rounds; dominated by highest-bit round

validation_criteria.qpe_check: result includes ancilla qubit count and number of IQPE rounds
validation_criteria.comparison_check: result includes VQE vs QPE/Krylov resource comparison

key_scientific_facts: The Be 2s-2p near-degeneracy is the largest correlation energy per active electron of any 2-electron active-space system.
CAS(2,4)/6-31G correlation energy (18.9 mHa) captures ~96% of total FCI/6-31G correlation (19.7 mHa); the remaining 0.8 mHa is from virtual orbitals beyond {2s,2p}.
IQPE with m=12 rounds resolves energies to precision 2⁻¹² × 5.0 Ha ≈ 1.2 mHa, just within chemical accuracy.
The Hartree-Fock reference for Be has |⟨HF|ψ₀⟩|² ≈ 0.847: QPE succeeds ≈85% of the time per shot — acceptable, but the multi-reference character slightly impairs QPE efficiency.
The quantum Krylov approach with 5 vectors typically achieves chemical accuracy for Be(2e,4o) with only ~5,000 total shots — the most efficient approach for this system.
common_failure_modes: Using full QPE (12 ancilla qubits, 20 total qubits) instead of IQPE (1 ancilla, 9 total).
Reporting qubit_count = 8 without including the IQPE ancilla qubit.
Not computing the HF initial state overlap (0.847) and its QPE success probability implication.
Using 6-31G** (polarisation + diffuse) instead of 6-31G (the specified basis).

tasks.physical_system: Heisenberg XXZ spin chain, 6 sites, open boundary, anisotropy Δ varied from 0 to 2

scientific_information.geometry: 6 spin-1/2 sites, OBC. H_XXZ = J Σᵢ[XᵢXᵢ₊₁ + YᵢYᵢ₊₁ + ΔZᵢZᵢ₊₁], J=1. Study at Δ ∈ {0.0, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0}.
scientific_information.hamiltonian: Not provided. Solver must write the explicit 6-qubit Pauli form.
scientific_information.reference_energy: Not provided. Solver must compute by exact diagonalisation.

tasks.prompt: Independently formulate the 6-qubit XXZ Hamiltonian for all 5 Δ values, compute exact-diagonalisation references, design a symmetry-adapted VQE ansatz, run VQE for each Δ, and report all seven required outputs for Δ=1.0 as primary.
tasks.benchmark_rationale: Most demanding S3 task: 5-parameter-point sweep, full independent reference computation, quantum-phase-transition analysis, and convergence difficulty near the BKT critical point.

verified_reference_energies_6site_obc_J1.computation_method: numpy.linalg.eigh of the 64×64 XXZ Hamiltonian; take the lowest eigenvalue
verified_reference_energies_6site_obc_J1.important_note: Values above are approximate. The solver MUST compute exact values numerically using the 6-site Hamiltonian matrix.

yang_baxter_TDL_Delta1.deviation: 5.4% above TDL due to finite-size boundary effects

XY_model_Delta0_exact.method: Free-fermion (JW transform + Fourier + diagonal): E₀ = −J Σₖ |ε_k| where ε_k = 2J cos(πk/(N+1)) for k=1,...,N/2

hamiltonian_formulation.key_insight: The XXZ Hamiltonian H = J Σ[XX+YY+ΔZZ] uses Pauli operators directly; no JW transform needed for spin systems.
hamiltonian_formulation.Sz_conservation: The XXZ model conserves Sz_total = Σ Zᵢ/2. Ground state lies in Sz_total=0 sector for even N.

measurement_grouping.note: Can reduce to 3 circuits by jointly rotating XX and YY groups via Rx(π/2) basis change

ansatz_recommendations.XY_phase_Delta_0: Matchgate circuit (Givens rotations): conserves Sz, matches free-fermion structure. 5 Givens angles (one per bond) = 5 parameters.

Heisenberg_critical_Delta_1.ansatz: QAOA-inspired p=3 layers: exp(−iγ H_ZZ) × exp(−iβ (H_XX+H_YY)), 6 parameters
Heisenberg_critical_Delta_1.alternative: Symmetry-adapted hardware-efficient circuit in Sz=0 sector, 2–3 layers
Heisenberg_critical_Delta_1.barren_plateau_note: At the BKT critical point Δ=1, the entanglement entropy grows as (1/3)ln(N) → deeper circuits needed and gradient norms decay

ansatz_recommendations.Neel_phase_Delta_2: Initial Néel state |↑↓↑↓↑↓⟩ = |101010⟩ + small QAOA p=1 corrections. Rapidly convergent due to finite gap.
ansatz_recommendations.symmetry_constraint: All ansätze must conserve Sz_total=0 (use XX+YY rotation gates which preserve magnetisation)

convergence_analysis.XY_phase: Gapless; COBYLA converges in ~100 evaluations with p=2 layers
convergence_analysis.BKT_critical_Delta_1: Gapless with logarithmic entanglement growth; gradient norms decay O(1/poly(N)). Expect 3–5× more evaluations and random restarts needed.
convergence_analysis.Neel_phase: Gapped (gap opens for Δ>1); rapid convergence from Néel initial state in ~50 evaluations

gate_count_p3.detail: 15 two-qubit blocks × 2 CNOTs each = 30 CNOTs per p-layer

validation_criteria.all_5_Delta_values: result must include energies for all 5 Δ values with corresponding exact-diag references
validation_criteria.convergence_analysis: result must discuss why Δ=1 is harder to converge than Δ=0 or Δ=2

key_scientific_facts: The XXZ model is exactly solvable via the Bethe Ansatz; at Δ=1 the ground-state energy per site in TDL is E₀/N = J(1/4 − ln 2) ≈ −0.4431J.
At Δ=0 (XY model), the XXZ chain is equivalent to free spinless fermions via JW; E₀ can be computed analytically from free-fermion dispersion.
The BKT phase transition at Δ=1 is infinite-order: the spin gap opens as ∝ exp(−c/√(Δ−1)) for Δ→1⁺, making finite-size signatures very weak.
The XXZ Hamiltonian directly uses Pauli operators X, Y, Z on qubits; no JW transform is required (the same key insight as the TFIM task).
For N=6 sites OBC with S_z=0 ground state at Δ=1: the half-chain von Neumann entropy S_vN ≈ (c/3)ln(N/2) + const ≈ 0.60 nats, reflecting the gapless Luttinger liquid structure.
common_failure_modes: Confusing Pauli spin operators (coefficient J in XᵢXⱼ) with spin-1/2 operators (which would have coefficient J/4); the Hamiltonian H = J Σ(XX+YY+ΔZZ) uses Pauli operators, not S=σ/2.
Not restricting the ansatz to the Sz_total=0 sector, causing the optimiser to explore non-physical magnetisation sectors.
Using the TDL Bethe Ansatz energy per site (−0.4431) as the 6-site OBC reference (differs by 5.4%).
Computing exact diagonalisation for only the primary Δ=1 case and not the other 4 values that the prompt requires.
